ev.q: In 2020, approximately 3,358,814 deaths occurred in the United States
From 2019 to 2020, the estimated age-adjusted death rate increased by 15.9%, from 715.2 to 828.7
Death rates were lowest among persons aged 5–14 years (13.6)
age-adjusted death rates were higher among males (990.5) than among females (689.2)
COVID-19 was reported as the underlying cause of death or a contributing cause of death for an estimated 377,883 (11.3%)
The age-adjusted rate was 828.7 deaths per 100,000 population
Overall age-adjusted death rates were lowest among Asian (457.9 per 100,000 population) and Hispanic persons (724.1)
Age-adjusted death rates were calculated for deaths by sex and race/ethnicity
CDC analyzed provisional NVSS death certificate data for deaths occurring among U.S. residents
To describe the trend in deaths during 2020
Age-adjusted death rates for 2020 were also compared with those from 2019

methods_quotes.q: Midyear U.S. Census Bureau population estimates (July 1, 2020) were used to calculate estimated death rates per 100,000 standard population
Age-adjusted death rates were calculated for deaths by sex and race/ethnicity, and crude death rates were calculated by age.
Age-adjusted death rates for 2020 were also compared with those from 2019
To describe the trend in deaths during 2020, the number of deaths from all causes and from COVID-19 were calculated for each week.
Age-adjusted death rates are provided by sex and race/ethnicity.
